llm.summary: The skill does medical-record structuring, but it also ships an unbounded self-evolution daemon and makes overstated privacy claims around sensitive medical data.

dimensions.detail: Reading user-supplied medical files and using billing network calls fit the stated purpose, but plaintext output of full medical records, raw source_text retention in results, and raw user ID trial tracking are not proportionate to the documented privacy posture.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation guidance uses normal local setup and environment variables, and I found no cron or service installer that automatically launches the daemon; however, the package includes a manually runnable indefinite daemon with a hardcoded installed-skill path.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime and security documentation under-disclose the self-modifying behavior and overstate protections, including claims that PHI is encrypted, not stored, and that user IDs are hashed despite code paths that do not enforce those guarantees.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists trial data under ~/.openclaw and, if the daemon is run, persists logs while continually mutating installed skill files; no root escalation was found, but the lifecycle and mutation authority are high impact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core parser and SkillPay billing are purpose-aligned, but auto-evolve-daemon.sh and scripts/self_evolve.py repeatedly rewrite executable code and SKILL.md, which is not needed for medical-record structuring.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this package carefully before installing. Do not run the auto-evolution daemon, avoid processing real PHI unless you have your own privacy controls, and treat the advertised encryption, hashing, audit logging, and no-storage claims as unsupported by the inspected code paths.
llm.findings:
[RA1] unexpected: Confirmed: auto-evolve-daemon.sh runs scripts/self_evolve.py in an infinite 30-minute loop; this is not required for the declared medical-record processing purpose.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Confirmed: scripts/self_evolve.py can modify scripts/process_record.py, SKILL.md, CHANGELOG.md, generated modules, and evolution-log.json without an approval or review gate.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed in part: demo messaging and security documentation imply simulated/local-only or protected handling, while user-supplied text is processed and complete source text can appear in outputs.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Confirmed: the tool handles PHI and can print or write complete records including metadata.source_text to plaintext output, while examples and integration snippets provide limited secure-handling guidance.
[PE3] expected: Downgraded: README.md mentions copying .env.example to .env for API keys, which is normal configuration documentation rather than evidence of credential theft.
[SC2] expected: Downgraded: scripts/upload-to-clawhub.sh uses curl to POST a skill package to an API; I did not find remote script fetching or execution in that file.
[RA2] expected: Partly downgraded: trial tracking state under ~/.openclaw is disclosed and related to free-trial enforcement, but it stores raw user IDs and timestamps rather than the documented hashed identifiers.
[PE2] expected: Downgraded: the cited chmod 755 troubleshooting command does not invoke sudo or root privileges.
[T06] unexpected: Confirmed: the daemon runs indefinitely and repeatedly invokes self-modifying code, although I did not find an automatic startup installer.
[T07] unexpected: Confirmed: the self-evolution code is non-idempotent and the artifact already contains many repeated lru_cache imports plus a long evolution log.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed: complete medical input can be included in plaintext output files, raw user IDs are persisted/transmitted for billing, and an API key can be supplied through command-line arguments.
